title: Startup Services (Enable / Disable)
definition: Configuring services to automatically start when the Linux operating system boots up.
simpleExplanation: Telling a program 'Turn yourself on automatically every time the server restarts, so I don't have to log in and do it manually.'
realWorldExample: A company server reboots after a power outage. The website comes back online, but the database doesn't. The admin forgot to type `sudo systemctl enable postgresql` when they installed it. Because it wasn't 'enabled', it didn't start on boot.
useCases: Disabling bloatware to speed up boot times

basic: If you run `systemctl enable nginx`, does it instantly turn Nginx on right then and there?
intermediate: How do you check a list of every single service configured to run at startup?

answers.question: Does it turn it on now?
answers.answer: No. `enable` ONLY tells Linux to start the service on the *next* boot. To start it immediately AND on boot, you must run `systemctl enable --now nginx`.
